input_params.description: Systematically explore the Ca/Si/Al/O composition space to identify the specific ratios that induce geometric frustration and probe the percolation transition in probe accessibility. This involves generating representative glass structures across the compositional range, computing their elastic properties to quantify the "effective rigidity," and analyzing the structural connectivity to validate the percolation-like behavior. The workflow will use the mechanical_properties skill to compute elastic moduli and the md_pipeline to generate equilibrated amorphous structures for analysis.
input_params.expected_prediction: The exploration will reveal a non-monotonic trend in the bulk/shear modulus versus composition, with a pronounced minimum (softening) at specific Ca/Si/Al/O ratios corresponding to the predicted geometric frustration zone. The modulus will recover on either side of this critical threshold, supporting the percolation-transition hypothesis. The effective rigidity will be quantitatively linked to the network connectivity metrics (e.g., bridging oxygen fraction).
